findings.title: Direct mutation of scene objects bypasses scene invariants
findings.message: The rotate command edits the scene's Objects slice in place. If canvas.Scene keeps a spatial index, cached bounds or a dirty flag, hit-testing and rendering will not see the new size. The swap also only changes Width and Height, so it never updates the object's X/Y or the scene revision. The inspector and the GPU board can end up disagreeing.
findings.suggestion: Update the object through a canvas.Scene method (for example an Update or SetObject call) that refreshes its index, or call the scene's invalidate or rebuild step after the mutation. Also invalidate the window so the change is drawn.

findings.title: Smoke test relies on fixed sleep and unchecked pixel coordinates
findings.message: The GPU smoke check waits a fixed 2 seconds and then reads a pixel at a computed screen position. It races with first render and with the --exit-after timer. If the app has closed, or the point falls outside the snapshot after zoom-in and fit, NRGBAAt returns a zero pixel and the check panics. That makes the smoke test flaky and can hang or crash on a closed app.
findings.suggestion: Trigger the snapshot after a frame has been rendered, for example from a render-complete callback, or poll with a bounded retry. Check that the point lies inside img.Bounds() before reading it, and stop the goroutine when the app closes.
